sources.prompt: Production game material atlas style edit. Image1 is the current material atlas: preserve EXACT four columns x four rows and every cell's material type and broad scale. Row1 four subtly varied worn limestone path slab patterns; row2 grass, sand, turquoise water, corral earth; row3 oak floorboards, walnut floorboards, warm plaster, terracotta shingles; row4 grey road, mossy cobbles, straw weave, aged timber. Entire surface fills every cell edge to edge, no borders, gutters, labels, props, people, text or perspective. Individually seamless repeatable texture in EACH cell: matching opposite edges, especially water, grass and sand; uniform overall illumination across each cell to prevent visible repeating squares. Clean large forms, subtle restrained hand-authored grain only where helpful; intentional two/three color material shading, gentle natural highlights, no tiny speckles, no gritty photographic detail, no random brushnoise, no muddy gradients or bevelled UI squares. Stone should have a few subtle irregular seam lines and muted moss, wood few carefully drawn grain lines. Gentle ambient crevice shading but no directional shadow across entire tiles. Clean readable production game materials, not generic flat solid swatches. Keep all16types in exact original order.

sources.name: props
sources.prompt: Style edit of production game prop atlas. Image1 contains sixteen props: preserve every object's identity, orientation, relative placement and EXACT four columns by four rows grid, each isolated with at least10% clear padding, no objects touch across cells. Redraw ALL16 props to match this refined stylized anime game style, removing gritty wear, speckled watercolor texture, dense micro-detail and plastic shine. CRITICAL SPACING CORRECTION: scale each of the sixteen individual props down to approximately65% of its current cell footprint.
